clue.text: Crazy with love about one king emperor

indicators.note: about means going around, so the crazy-plus-love pair wraps the next two pieces

parts.note: crazy means mad
one is the Roman numeral I
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovestruck madman circles a monarch who styles himself emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IK inside MADO, splitting it as M-IK-ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was used in the West for the hereditary ruler of Japan, a monarch of imperial rank.

clue.text: Peak in wrong place makes one sort of cross

indicators.note: in places the word for a peak inside the rearranged letters
wrong signals that the letters of place are put out of order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A mountain top in the wrong spot somehow produces a kind of crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 'place' as PECAL. A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England, such as on Dartmoor; 'Peak' looks like the definition, but 'one sort of cross' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral cross is the large crucifix a bishop wears hanging on the chest.

clue.text: All company may have to offer before end of year

definitions.text: All company may have to offer before end of year

parts.words: All company may have to offer before end of year
parts.note: a firm's shareholders may be paid a part-payout on profits midway through the financial year, ahead of the final one

explanation.surface: Every business may be obliged to make some offer before December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All company' reads as every firm, but it is any limited company paying its shareholders a share of profits partway through the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is a share of profits paid to shareholders; the provisional one before the year's accounts are final is called this.

indicators.note: protecting means guarding around, so the agent's word encloses the band's

parts.note: an agent in espionage is a spy
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A secret agent acts as bodyguard to a music band, proving tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that bounces back into shape after being pressed.

parts.note: a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise in a wall, but here it is the litter that carries a sick person, and its porter moves the invalid along

explanation.surface: A builder's labourer hauling bricks makes sure things move on steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective meaning unhurried; it is the person in hospital being carried.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the porter, often in wartime, who carries the wounded or sick on a litter.

clue.text: After this double blow, start to count boxer out?

definitions.text: After this double blow, start to count boxer out?

parts.words: After this double blow, start to count boxer out?
parts.note: a quick left-and-right combination punch, and also the first two numbers a referee calls when counting a floored fighter

explanation.surface: Following a two-punch combination, the referee begins counting the fighter out.
explanation.walkthrough: The combination punch and the referee's opening numbers share one name, so the punch leads straight into the count.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a jab followed quickly by a cross with the other fist is known by this name.

clue.text: One may back up to this handle

definitions.text: One may back up to this
definitions.meaning: to back someone up to the ... is to support them completely
the grip of a sword or dagger

explanation.walkthrough: 'back up' suggests reversing a vehicle; it means support, in the idiom of backing someone to the full.
explanation.definitionFit: The grip of a sword reaches as far as a blade can go in, giving the idiom of total support.

definitions.meaning: to hold out a gift is to offer or hand it over
to yield is to bend or collapse under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both offering something to someone and buckling or bending under pressure.

definitions.meaning: down here is the soft raised surface of fabric such as velvet
forty winks is a short sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like an adverb or feathers; it is the pile on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised fibres on velvet share a name with a short daytime doze.

clue.text: In can, girl found something from tea

indicators.note: In placed before can's word means the girl's name sits inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Inside a tin, a young woman discovered something left from her brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start reads as a preposition setting the scene, but it is the container signal; 'found' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This astringent plant compound gives brewed leaves their bitter, drying taste.

indicators.note: conceals means hides inside, so the fellow's word encloses the scripture's

parts.note: a fellow is a male
NT is the New Testament, a body of scripture

explanation.surface: A man hides a holy book inside his cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' is the container signal; 'Fellow' gives MALE, not MAN, which is the false first move since MAN leaves no room for the scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name a loose sleeveless outer garment worn over the shoulders.

clue.text: Personality may be sort of card

definitions.meaning: personality here is one's individual self
a card carried to prove who one is

explanation.definitionFit: One's distinct individual self, and the card a person carries to prove who they are.

indicators.note: whence means out of which, so the solver draws the answer out of the following letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gossip gasps at the idea of schoolgirls running away from their dorms.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GIRLS ABSCOND OOH rearrange to give the answer, while the whole clue asks where girls might run away from.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils of residential schools live there in term time, so it is a place they might run off from.

definitions.meaning: to enter data is to record it in a record book
a piece of cut tree trunk for the fire

explanation.definitionFit: To record something in a journal, and a cut length of tree trunk for burning.

indicators.note: protects means shields around, so the dog's word wraps the daughter's letter

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: The family dog shields a little girl when there is an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' puts D inside COLLIE, giving COLLI-D-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe two moving things smashing into one another.

clue.text: Fifty missing in lake, Scotsman may cry

indicators.note: missing means the Roman fifty is dropped from the lake's word

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims after fifty people go missing in a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes L out of LOCH. The answer is a Scottish exclamation, like 'oh'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish interjection expresses surprise or regret, the kind of exclamation a Scot might utter.

clue.text: Bungle, taking long time for errand

parts.note: to make a mess of something is to bungle it
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone botches a task and takes ages over a simple errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bungle' looks like a verb, but it supplies the noun MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense, still alive in Scotland, means a commission or trip to carry out on someone's behalf.

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: University tutors cried when they were made to quit their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges DONS WEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a post or office is to resign from it, the same as giving up a job.

parts.note: O is a nil score, nothing
ST is short for street, a way
rich food is full-flavoured

explanation.surface: Asks whether a bird could possibly be tasty and full of flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in no way' reads as never; it splits as O (nothing) and ST (street).
explanation.definitionFit: This large flightless African runner is the biggest living feathered creature.

clue.text: I wouldn't see him as an h g wells character

definitions.text: I wouldn't see him as an h g wells character

parts.words: I wouldn't see him as an h g wells character
parts.note: the speaker could not see this figure at all, since the Wells novel's scientist cannot be seen

explanation.surface: Someone says they cannot picture him as a figure from an H G Wells story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wouldn't see him as' sounds like a view on casting, but it means literally could not see him. H G Wells wrote the 1897 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells's 1897 novel follows the scientist Griffin, who makes his own body impossible to see.

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of ruined are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has grown used to being dreadfully wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges RUINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hardened through long exposure to something unpleasant is to be used to it.

definitions.meaning: split in two, the word says I am in use, that is, employed

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works only when the answer is broken into two words saying the speaker is being put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being diverted or tickled, and, split in two, being put to work.

definitions.meaning: the joint between arm and torso
to bear a burden is to take its weight

explanation.walkthrough: 'body of bear' suggests an animal's anatomy, but 'of' is a link and 'bear' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint where the arm meets the torso, and taking on responsibility or weight.

definitions.meaning: a preliminary qualifying race or contest

explanation.definitionFit: Fervour or intensity of feeling, and a preliminary qualifying race whose winners go through.

clue.text: A way to lead our enthusiasm

indicators.note: to lead means to go in front of, so the first pieces come before the last word

parts.note: RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Finding a way to guide our keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead' puts the first pieces in front, read as going ahead of 'our'; 'way' is the usual crossword road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean fervent eagerness or passion for something.

indicators.note: production of suggests making something new from the letters of the word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Allowing whalebone to be manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges ENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plates some whales use to filter food were once used for corset stays under this name.

clue.text: Told to wait patiently for signal

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word for waiting in line is heard rather than written

parts.note: to queue is to wait patiently in line

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to hold on quietly until given the sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told' signals sound: QUEUE, waiting in line (a very British habit), sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's prompt word or a sign to begin speaking or acting.

clue.text: Make keen and hot in feeble surroundings

indicators.note: in places the hot letter inside the feeble word
surroundings confirms the feeble word wraps round the letter for hot

parts.note: wet is British slang for a feeble, ineffectual person
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Sharpening something while hot amid weak, damp conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in feeble surroundings' puts H inside WET. 'Wet' as British slang means feeble or spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: To sharpen an appetite or a blade, so make it keener.
